name: Cathedral Basilica of St. Joseph
history: The first church on this site, San José de Guadalupe (1803), was California's first parish built for Spanish settlers rather than a mission. An adobe church followed in the 1830s-40s, and a later church burned in 1875. The present church was dedicated in 1877; the portico was finished in 1884 and the dome in 1885. After a restoration it became the cathedral of the new Diocese of San José, completed in 1990.
arch: A classical temple front with columns and pediment, two towers and a large central dome over a cross-shaped church.
features: Latin verses from the Gospel of Matthew about St. Joseph run along the top of the interior walls.
It faces the city's old plaza, now Plaza de César Chávez.

look.d: Finished in 1885, it crowns downtown San Jose.
The columned front was completed in 1884.

fun: San Jose is named for St. Joseph, the church's patron.
journal: On the old pueblo plaza: a parish older than the state of California.
